### 1. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) Boilerplate

```R
# ==============================================================================
# EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS (EDA) BOILERPLATE
# ==============================================================================

# 1. LOAD LIBRARIES
# -------------------
# Use suppressPackageStartupMessages to prevent package loading warnings in reports
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
  library(skimr)          # For quick data summaries
  library(janitor)        # For data cleaning utilities
  library(readr)          # For fast CSV/Excel reading
  library(corrplot)       # For correlation heatmaps
  library(ggrepel)        # For enhanced labeling on plots
})

# 2. ENVIRONMENT CONFIGURATION
# ----------------------------
# Set up warnings and reproducibility
options(warn = 1)           # Treat warnings as errors (adjust as needed)
set.seed(42)                # Ensures reproducibility in random steps

# 3. DATA LOADING FUNCTIONS
# -------------------------
# Define variables for input paths
DATA_FILE <- "data.csv"    # Replace with your file path
DELIMITER <- ","           # Replace if your file uses tab/semicolon
SHEET_NAME <- "Sheet1"    # Replace if reading Excel

# Function to load data safely
load_data <- function(filepath, sheet = NULL) {
  if (file.exists(filepath)) {
    message(paste("Loading data from:", filepath))
    # Read CSV
    data <- readr::read_csv(filepath, col_types = readr::cols(), show_col_types =
TRUE)
  } else {
    message("Warning: File not found. Creating dummy data structure.")
    data <- tibble::tibble(a = c(1,2,3), b = c(4,5,6))
  }
  return(data)
}

# 4. INITIAL INSPECTION
# ---------------------
check_data <- function(df) {
  # Store metadata for reporting
  message("Running Initial Data Check...")

  # Basic Dimension Check
  message(paste("Columns:", ncol(df)))
  message(paste("Rows:", nrow(df)))

  # Check Column Types (skimr does this automatically, but we show it explicitly)
  col_types <- colnames(df)
  # Convert to data.frame with explicit types for consistency
  col_dfs <- as.list(df)

  # Identify unique types
  types <- sapply(col_dfs, class)
  message("Column Types:\n")
  print(as.data.frame(types))

  # Identify unique values count (unique rows per column)
  unique_counts <- col_dfs %>% sapply(n_distinct) %>% unlist()
  message("Unique Counts per Column:\n")
  print(as.data.frame(unique_counts))

  return(df)
}

# 5. DATA CLEANING (Optional Pre-processing)
# ------------------------------------------
clean_data <- function(df) {
  message("Cleaning Data...")

  # Convert character columns to factors if needed (e.g., categorical columns)
  # (Logic depends on your specific column structure, use caution)
  # Example: df <- df %>% mutate(id = as.character(id))

  # Remove rows with critical missing values
  # (Adjust threshold or logic based on EDA goals)
  message("Checking Missing Values...")
  df %>% summarize(missing_count = sum(is.na(.)))

  return(df)
}

# 6. DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
# --------------------------
describe_data <- function(df) {
  message("Generating Descriptive Statistics...")

  # Basic summary using summary()
  summary_stats <- summarize_stats(df,
                                    numeric = "numeric",
                                    categorical = "categorical")

  return(summary_stats)
}

# Helper to summarize numeric and categorical data
summarize_stats <- function(df, numeric = NULL, categorical = NULL) {
  # Separate numeric and categorical
  num_vars <- subset(df, select = where(is.numeric)) %>% summarize(n = nrow(df))
  cat_vars <- subset(df, select = where(is.factor | is.character)) %>% summarize(n
= nrow(df))

  cat("=== Numeric Summary ===\n")
  print(summary(df %>% select(where(is.numeric))))
  cat("\n=== Categorical Summary ===\n")
  print(table(df %>% select(where(is.factor | is.character))) %>% as.data.frame)

  return(NULL)
}

# 7. VISUALIZATION
# ----------------
plot_data <- function(df, x_var = NULL, y_var = NULL) {
  message("Generating Visualizations...")

  # Histogram for numeric columns
  num_cols <- df %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% colnames()

  # Loop through columns to create histograms
  for (col in num_cols) {
    p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = !!enquo(col), fill = factor(col))) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "white") +
      labs(title = paste("Distribution:", col),
           x = col, y = "Count") +
      theme_minimal()

    print(p)
    message("Generated Histogram for: ", col)
  }

  # Boxplot for comparison
  cat_vars <- df %>% select(where(is.factor | is.character)) %>% colnames()
  if (length(cat_vars) > 0) {
    message("Generating Boxplot for Categorical Variables...")
    # Example: Boxplot for specific numeric col vs Categorical factor
    # (Logic depends on column names)
  }
}

# 8. CORRELATION ANALYSIS
# -----------------------
compute_correlation <- function(df) {
  message("Computing Correlations...")

  # Extract numeric columns only
  num_vars <- subset(df, select = where(is.numeric))

  # Correlation matrix
  cor_matrix <- cor(num_vars, use = "complete.obs")

  message("Correlation Matrix:\n")
  print(cor_matrix)

  # Visualization
  plot <- ggcorrplot(as.matrix(cor_matrix),
                     main = "Correlation Heatmap")
  print(plot)

  return(cor_matrix)
}

# 9. EXECUTION SCRIPT
# -------------------
# Run the pipeline
main_EDA <- function() {
  # Load Data
  # Note: This step is where you replace the dummy data with your real dataset
  data <- load_data(DATA_FILE)

  # Step 1: Check Data
  data <- check_data(data)

  # Step 2: Clean Data (Optional)
  # data <- clean_data(data)

  # Step 3: Describe
  summarize_stats(data)

  # Step 4: Visualize
  # plot_data(data)

  # Step 5: Correlation
  # compute_correlation(data)
}

# RUN MAIN
if (!interactive()) {
  main_EDA()
}
```
